pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #2 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the lesson of the hare and tortoise story? (1 mark)
   A. Hares are lazy
   B. Tortoises are fast
   C. Never race
   D. Slow and steady wins the race

2. Which is a part of an oral narrative? (1 mark)
   A. A page number
   B. A stamp
   C. The ending
   D. A price tag

3. Why do we explain a proverb in our own words? (1 mark)
   A. To hide it
   B. To make it longer
   C. To show we understand the lesson
   D. To change it forever

4. In The farmer was weary after a long day in the shamba, weary means (1 mark)
   A. very loud
   B. very hungry
   C. very tired
   D. very rich

5. What is the setting of a story? (1 mark)
   A. The last line
   B. The name of the writer
   C. Where and when it happens
   D. The price

6. What is an imaginative composition? (1 mark)
   A. A list of prices
   B. A news report
   C. A weather forecast
   D. A story made from the imagination

7. How should you speak when narrating an event? (1 mark)
   A. Angrily always
   B. Without stopping
   C. Clearly and with feeling
   D. Very quietly

8. Which sentence uses when correctly? (1 mark)
   A. We when ran.
   B. When we ran home rained it.
   C. Rained we when home.
   D. When it rained, we ran home.

9. Where can the main idea often be found? (1 mark)
   A. In the first sentence of a paragraph
   B. Only in the last word
   C. In the page number
   D. Nowhere

10. What is a service? (1 mark)
   A. A market
   B. Work done for others
   C. A kind of coin
   D. A thing you can hold

11. Which group of words is a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. The customer pays fifty shillings.
   B. The customer in the market
   C. Fifty shillings
   D. Pays fifty

12. Which word shows a choice? (1 mark)
   A. or
   B. and
   C. so
   D. but

13. The ball is touching the top of the table. Which preposition fits? (1 mark)
   A. outside
   B. behind
   C. under
   D. on

14. Which preposition needs two things to make sense? (1 mark)
   A. under
   B. on
   C. in
   D. between

15. What does pace mean when reading a poem? (1 mark)
   A. How long the poem is
   B. How many words rhyme
   C. How fast or slow you read
   D. How loud you read

16. Which pair of words rhyme? (1 mark)
   A. water and food
   B. day and play
   C. hen and goat
   D. cow and shade

17. What is spoken word? (1 mark)
   A. Poetry performed aloud for an audience
   B. A dictionary
   C. A kind of drawing
   D. A silent song

18. What are the events of a story? (1 mark)
   A. The author
   B. The title
   C. What happens step by step
   D. The margin

19. What should you do first when studying a picture for a story? (1 mark)
   A. Write the ending
   B. Copy a story
   C. Look at the whole picture
   D. Cover it

20. How should peer feedback be given? (1 mark)
   A. Loudly
   B. Never
   C. Kindly, with one good point and one suggestion
   D. Rudely

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Give three money words and their meanings. (3 marks)

22. Plan a short oral narrative about a school rule. Say the characters, the events, the ending, and where you will use a simile and a metaphor. (5 marks)

23. What is a conjunction? Give one example. (2 marks)

24. Plan a story that uses the proverb Many hands make light work. Give the title, characters, problem and ending. (4 marks)

25. Describe how a class can start a reading club. (4 marks)

26. State three benefits of reading widely. (3 marks)

27. Describe the steps in writing a story from a picture. (4 marks)

28. Write a paragraph of four sentences about a time you handled money. Use when at least twice. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #2 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Slow and steady wins the race
   The tortoise wins by steady effort.

2. C — The ending
   Stories have openings, characters, events and endings.

3. C — To show we understand the lesson
   Explaining shows understanding of the meaning.

4. C — very tired
   A long day of work suggests tiredness.

5. C — Where and when it happens
   Setting means place and time.

6. D — A story made from the imagination
   Imaginative compositions are made-up stories.

7. C — Clearly and with feeling
   Clear speech and feeling make a story good.

8. D — When it rained, we ran home.
   It shows two events joined by time.

9. A — In the first sentence of a paragraph
   First sentences often give the main idea.

10. B — Work done for others
   Cutting hair is a service.

11. A — The customer pays fifty shillings.
   It has a subject and a predicate.

12. A — or
   Or offers a choice.

13. D — on
   On shows contact with the top.

14. D — between
   Between means with something on each side.

15. C — How fast or slow you read
   Pace is speed.

16. B — day and play
   Day and play end in the same sound.

17. A — Poetry performed aloud for an audience
   Spoken word is performed poetry.

18. C — What happens step by step
   Events are the actions in order.

19. C — Look at the whole picture
   First see the whole picture.

20. C — Kindly, with one good point and one suggestion
   Kind feedback helps writers.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Trade: buying and selling. Profit: money gained. Customer: person who buys. Price: cost of something.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each word with its meaning.

22. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any plan with characters, events in order, an ending with a lesson, and one simile and one metaphor, for example a pupil who came late but learned that rules are like a map.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for characters, events, ending, simile and metaphor.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: A conjunction is a joining word, such as and, but or when.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for an example.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any suitable plan, for example Title: The Clean Compound. Characters: pupils. Problem: a dirty compound. Ending: everyone helps and it is clean quickly.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Collect books, choose a name and a librarian, agree on rules for borrowing, meet regularly to read and share books, and record who borrowed each book.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four correct points.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: It builds vocabulary, improves spelling, gives new ideas, makes you a better writer and speaker, gives enjoyment.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each benefit.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: Look at the whole picture, ask who where and what, plan the characters, setting, problem and ending, write the story in order, and check it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

28. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four clear sentences with two uses of when, for example When I reached the shop, I counted my money. When I paid, I received change. I was happy.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each clear sentence and one mark for correct use of when.
